title: Layer-not-found pull failures across the Ferrolith registry fleet
domain: container image registry and garbage collection
summary: Northmark Systems runs Ferrolith, a self-hosted container image registry, at six production sites. Since mid-June 2026 image pulls have intermittently returned a 404 naming a layer that storage no longer holds, even though the images passed push-time verification. Site configurations differ along several axes and a vendor advisory has already named a cause. Determine what produces the failures and what to do about it.

entities.name: Ferrolith Registry 3.4
entities.note: Self-hosted container image registry with a blob garbage collector.

entities.name: SYD-1
entities.note: Sydney production registry site, pinned to an older release.

entities.name: stg-1
entities.note: Shared staging registry used for reproduction work.

entities.name: Ferrolith blob collector
entities.note: Marks reachable blobs and sweeps the rest.

entities.name: Ferrolith replication worker
entities.note: Materializes blobs from origin sites into replica sites.

entities.name: Cirrus S3-compatible object store
entities.note: Blob storage backend at some sites.

entities.name: Vantage 2.1 proxy
entities.note: TLS-terminating reverse proxy in front of the registry.

entities.name: v2 deduplication store

nodes.text: Concurrent mark-and-sweep collection enabled at a site.
Deferred pull-through blob replication enabled at a site.
Stop-the-world collection write barrier held across the mark phase.
The v2 deduplication store enabled at a site.
The 3.4 metadata index migration executed at a site.
The Cirrus backend running behind the Vantage 2.1 proxy build at a site.
A blob reference row created after the mark-phase snapshot was taken.
The sweep phase deleting blobs the snapshot recorded as unreferenced.
Elevated replica blob-fetch latency during the incident window.

evidence.text: Incident summary IR-4471: since 2026-06-11 image pulls across the Ferrolith fleet have intermittently returned HTTP 404 naming a layer digest that the blob store no longer holds. Twenty-six tickets were filed this quarter. Every affected image passed push-time manifest and layer verification when it was originally pushed.

Fleet baseline: in the fourteen months before the 3.4 upgrade, when every site ran stop-the-world collection, the fleet recorded zero layer-not-found tickets. Both replication configurations in use today were already in use at some sites during that period.
Collection-mode inventory as of 2026-08-20: concurrent mark-and-sweep collection is enabled at IAD-3, SIN-2, ORD-2, FRA-1 and DUB-4. SYD-1 is pinned to release 3.3 and runs stop-the-world collection.

Replication-mode inventory as of 2026-08-20: deferred pull-through replication is configured at IAD-3, SIN-2 and SYD-1. ORD-2, FRA-1 and DUB-4 use eager replication, which fetches every blob before the manifest row is written.
Ticket origin breakdown for the twenty-six tickets: twenty-four originated at IAD-3 and SIN-2; two originated at SYD-1. No ticket in this class originated at ORD-2, FRA-1 or DUB-4.

Reliability dashboard panel circulated to leadership: 92 percent of layer-not-found tickets this quarter (24 of 26) came from sites running concurrent collection. Concurrent collection was enabled at the five upgraded sites on 2026-06-08 and the first ticket arrived 2026-06-11. Vendor advisory VA-2026-118 attributes this error class to concurrent collection.

Ticket triage note on the two SYD-1 tickets: both were reclassified as authentication failures. The pulling cluster presented an expired registry credential and the 404 body was generated by the Vantage proxy rather than the registry. A storage audit at SYD-1 found every referenced layer present.
Post-upgrade operating record for ORD-2, FRA-1 and DUB-4: sixty-one combined site-weeks since the 3.4 upgrade with zero confirmed layer-not-found failures, across 1,180 collection cycles.

Post-upgrade operating record for SYD-1: nineteen site-weeks with zero confirmed layer-not-found failures once the two reclassified tickets are excluded. Its replication worker logs show blob reference rows written between four and fifty-one minutes after the corresponding manifest row.

Configuration history: deferred pull-through replication has been enabled at IAD-3, SIN-2 and SYD-1 continuously since March 2024. No layer-not-found ticket was filed at any of those three sites before June 2026.

Workload comparability review: weekly image push volume at ORD-2 and DUB-4 is within 12 percent of IAD-3 and SIN-2, and FRA-1 is within 9 percent. SYD-1 is within 20 percent. Tag churn and average layer count per manifest are comparable across all six sites.

Collector design note CD-19: concurrent collection computes a reachable-set snapshot when the mark phase begins and then sweeps every blob the snapshot recorded as unreferenced. References created after the snapshot are not re-checked before deletion in the same cycle. A blob becomes sweep-eligible once it has been resident and unreferenced for the grace window, measured from blob write time. Fleet settings are a six-hour grace window and a mark snapshot every six hours.

Replication design note CD-22: the deferred pull-through worker writes the manifest row first and creates blob reference rows only as each blob is materialized, which may be many minutes later and may attach to blob content already resident from an earlier cache fill. Eager replication creates the blob reference rows in the same transaction that writes the manifest row.

Collector design note CD-20: stop-the-world collection holds a registry-wide write barrier across the entire mark phase, so no reference row can be created between the snapshot and the sweep. The barrier suspends pushes and replication writes for the duration of the mark phase, which averaged thirty-eight minutes at current fleet scale.

Collector and replication log excerpt, IAD-3: blob sha256:9f3c1a written into the local store 2026-07-01 14:02 during a cache fill for an unrelated tag and unreferenced thereafter; mark snapshot taken 2026-07-02 01:58 recorded it unreferenced and past the grace window; replication worker created a reference to the same digest at 02:11 for manifest northmark/ingest-api:2026.07.1; sweep deleted the blob at 02:14; the first failing pull of that tag was logged at 06:40.

Collector log comparison, ORD-2: the same snapshot-then-sweep sequence runs on the same six-hour cadence and deletes a comparable volume of unreferenced blobs per cycle, with no subsequent pull failures recorded against any manifest referenced in those cycles.

Reproduction report RR-88 from the platform team: 'Reproduced layer-not-found in stg-1 with concurrent collection enabled; the same test on stop-the-world collection did not reproduce. Conclusion: concurrent collection is sufficient to cause the failure.'

Configuration snapshot for stg-1 covering the RR-88 test window: the staging site was provisioned from the IAD-3 profile template, with deferred pull-through replication enabled throughout both test runs.

Monitoring: SIN-2 raised clock-skew alarms reaching 340 milliseconds on 2026-06-19 and again on 2026-07-14. Collector snapshot timestamps and reference-row timestamps are both issued by the site's metadata database clock.

Capacity alerts: the IAD-3 blob volume crossed its 85 percent watermark on 2026-06-27 and triggered cache eviction. Evicted paths are pull-through cache paths, which are re-fetchable from the origin site on demand and are not registry-of-record storage.
Upgrade logs: the 3.4 metadata index migration emitted 1,412 'row rewritten' warnings at each of the five upgraded sites, including the three sites with no failures.

Migration follow-up: a full metadata reindex with checksum verification at IAD-3 on 2026-07-09 reported no inconsistencies, and layer-not-found failures continued at the prior rate for the following eight days.
Platform inventory: IAD-3 and SIN-2 both run the Cirrus S3-compatible backend behind the Vantage 2.1 proxy build. No other combination of backend and proxy build is shared by exactly those two sites.
Platform inventory continued: ORD-2 also runs the Cirrus S3-compatible backend behind the Vantage 2.1 proxy build and has recorded no confirmed layer-not-found failures since the upgrade.

Release note for Ferrolith 3.4.2: adds a write barrier covering in-flight client uploads during the mark phase. Reference rows created by the replication worker are explicitly listed as out of scope for the new barrier.
Field report: IAD-3 upgraded to 3.4.2 on 2026-08-04 and filed four further confirmed layer-not-found tickets in the following two weeks, at a rate consistent with the preceding period.

Telemetry gap: the replica blob-fetch latency series was dropped when the metrics retention policy changed on 2026-05-30. No latency data exists for any site during the incident window, the series cannot be backfilled from logs, and no other record of replica fetch duration was retained.

Deployment status of the v2 deduplication store: enabled only at SYD-1. Release 3.4 contains a configuration guard that refuses to start when the v2 store and concurrent collection are both enabled, and an organization-wide change freeze through Q4 blocks any further v2 store deployment. No site has ever run the v2 store together with concurrent collection.

Targeted change at SIN-2: on 2026-08-12 the site was switched from deferred to eager replication while remaining on concurrent collection. Zero confirmed layer-not-found tickets in the nine days since, at unchanged push volume and unchanged collection cadence.

Capacity proposal CP-207 from the storage team: cut the mark snapshot interval from six hours to one hour and set the blob grace window to zero, because unreferenced blobs occupy 18 percent of capacity at IAD-3 and the backlog is blamed for long mark phases. The proposal has not been implemented at any site.

Detection note: the pull-time layer integrity check is the only signal that a layer is missing. When it fires the registry returns 404 and records the manifest digest and the missing layer digest, which is how all twenty-four confirmed tickets were localized to a specific manifest and collection cycle.

Collector telemetry note: the grace window has been six hours at every site since the 3.4 upgrade and no site has ever operated at a different value. The collector does not record how long each swept blob had been resident, so the effect of a different window cannot be reconstructed from retained data at any site.

hypotheses.text: Concurrent mark-and-sweep collection, acting by itself, produces the layer-not-found pull failures seen at the affected sites.
Deferred pull-through replication, acting by itself, produces the layer-not-found pull failures seen at the affected sites.
Concurrent collection acting jointly with deferred replication produces the layer-not-found pull failures seen at the affected sites.
The Cirrus backend acting jointly with the Vantage proxy build produces the layer-not-found pull failures seen at the affected sites.
The 3.4 metadata index migration, acting by itself, produces the layer-not-found pull failures seen at the affected sites.
Expired cluster pull credentials, acting by themselves, produce the layer-not-found pull failures seen at the affected sites.
Concurrent collection acting jointly with the v2 deduplication store produces the layer-not-found pull failures seen at the affected sites.

observations.text: Concurrent collection is necessary for the confirmed layer-not-found failures: no confirmed failure occurs at a site without it.
Concurrent collection is sufficient for the confirmed layer-not-found failures: sites running it show the failures regardless of their other settings.
Deferred replication is necessary for the confirmed layer-not-found failures: no confirmed failure occurs at a site without it.
Deferred replication is sufficient for the confirmed layer-not-found failures: sites running it show the failures regardless of their other settings.
The rise in failures that followed enabling concurrent collection appears at sites using deferred replication and is absent at sites using eager replication.
Elevated replica blob-fetch latency combines with concurrent collection to produce the confirmed layer-not-found failures at the affected sites.

actions.text: Switch IAD-3 and SIN-2 from deferred to eager blob replication, leaving their collection mode unchanged, and track pull errors for two weeks.
Pin IAD-3 and SIN-2 to stop-the-world collection, leaving their replication mode unchanged, and track pull errors and push latency for two weeks.
Extend the 3.4.2 write barrier to cover replication-created reference rows, and validate the resulting build at one canary site before any fleet rollout.
Roll every site in the fleet back to stop-the-world collection on release 3.3, and hold the registry upgrade program until the next release train.
Move IAD-3 and SIN-2 off the Cirrus backend and roll their Vantage proxy build back, leaving collection and replication settings unchanged.
Cut the mark snapshot interval to one hour and set the blob grace window to zero fleet-wide, so each collection cycle tracks a smaller reference backlog.
Downgrade the pull-time layer integrity check to a warning and serve the last cached manifest when a layer is missing, so client pulls stop returning errors.
